title: Nanobind Extraction Protocol for Easily Fragmenting DNA
author: Giada Ferrari

steps.title: Tissue Preparation and Thawing
steps.instruction: Prepare the frozen tissue sample on ice or dry ice and thaw it in L buffer.

substeps.instruction: Cut a suitable piece of frozen tissue with a scalpel blade in a pre-cooled petri dish or weighing boat.
Immediately cover the sample with 1-5 mL of L buffer (10 mM Tris pH 7.6, 100 mM EDTA, 20 mM NaCl).
Allow the sample to thaw in the L buffer.
Mince the tissue into small pieces with a scalpel blade.
Collect the buffer and tissue pieces into microcentrifuge tubes.
If necessary, rinse the petri dish with L buffer and collect into the same tubes.

steps.title: Initial Pellet Recovery
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the sample to isolate the pellet and discard the supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 3,000 x g for 00:05:00.
Discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspension and Homogenization
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in Buffer CT and consolidate into a Protein LoBind tube.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend pellets using a total of 1 mL of cold Buffer CT by pipette mixing 10X with a wide bore P200 pipette.
Transfer all resuspended pellets into one 2 mL Protein LoBind microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 3,000 x g and 4°C for 00:05:00 to pellet homogenate.
Discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Protein Digestion
steps.instruction: Digest proteins using Proteinase K and Buffer CLE3.

substeps.instruction: Pulse vortex for 1s x 2 times (max setting) to dislodge the pellet.
Add 20 µL of Proteinase K to the pellet.
Add 150 µL of Buffer CLE3 and pipette mix 10X with a wide bore P200 pipette.
Incubate on a ThermoMixer at 55°C and 600 rpm for 00:20:00.
Spin the tube on a mini-centrifuge for 2 s to remove liquid from the cap.
Add 20 µL of RNase A.
Incubate on a ThermoMixer at 55°C and 600 rpm for 00:20:00.
Spin the tube on a mini-centrifuge for 2 s to remove liquid from the cap.

steps.title: Protein Precipitation and Lysate Recovery
steps.instruction: Precipitate remaining proteins and recover the supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Add 60 µL of Buffer SB and pulse vortex for 1s x 5 times (max setting) to mix.
Centrifuge at 10,000 x g and RT (15–30°C) for 00:05:00.
Transfer up to 300 µL of supernatant to a new 1.5 mL Protein LoBind microcentrifuge tube using a wide bore P200 pipette (discard the 2 mL tube containing the pellet).

steps.title: Nanobind Disk Binding
steps.instruction: Bind the DNA to the Nanobind disk using Buffer BL3 and isopropanol.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL of Buffer BL3 to the supernatant and inversion mix 10X.
Spin the tube on a mini-centrifuge for 2 s to remove liquid from the cap.
Add Nanobind disk to the lysate and add 350 µL of isopropanol.
Inversion mix 10X.
Mix on a platform rocker at 20 rpm for 00:15:00 at RT.

steps.title: DNA Washing
steps.instruction: Wash the DNA-bound Nanobind disk using magnetic separation.

substeps.instruction: Place tube rack on the magnetic base (per PacBio Nanobind tissue kit Guide).
Discard supernatant with a pipette, avoiding the DNA or the Nanobind disk.
Add 500 µL of Buffer CW1, remove from magnetic base, inversion mix 4X, replace on magnetic base, and discard supernatant.
Repeat the CW1 wash.
Add 500 µL of Buffer CW2, remove from magnetic base, inversion mix 4X, replace on magnetic base, and discard supernatant.
Repeat the CW2 wash.

steps.title: Residual Liquid Removal
steps.instruction: Remove all residual wash buffer from the tube.

substeps.instruction: Spin the tube on a mini-centrifuge for 2 s.
With the tube rack on the magnetic base and right-side-up, place the tube on the rack and remove residual liquid.
Repeat this process once more.
Remove tube from tube rack.

steps.title: DNA Elution
steps.instruction: Elute the DNA from the Nanobind disk using Buffer LTE.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL of Buffer LTE directly onto the Nanobind disk and incubate at RT for 00:10:00.
Collect DNA by transferring eluate to a new 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Spin the tube containing the Nanobind disk on a mini-centrifuge for 5 s.
Use a standard P200 pipette to combine any additional liquid from the disk with the eluate; repeat if necessary.

steps.title: Sample Homogenization
steps.instruction: Finalize the DNA sample by disrupting any unsolubilized material.

substeps.instruction: Pipette mix the sample 5X with a wide-bore 200 µL pipette tip to homogenize and disrupt any unsolubilized “jellies”.
Let the sample rest at RT overnight to allow DNA to solubilize.
